title: Epochal service key policy and host-bound ephemeral enforcement
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Background:
Redwood needs stronger guarantees around long-lived service credentials. Current service keys are variable in form, often missing environment scoping, and lack binding to host/process identity. This increases blast radius when keys are leaked and complicates automated revocation.

Goal:
- Define and enforce an "epochal" key policy (short cryptoperiods by default) for service keys.
- Introduce host-bound ephemeral tokens for VM/container workloads (bound to host fingerprint or instance identity).
- Standardize machine key naming to make discovery and audit easier.
- Surface rotation/expiry events in audit logs with structured fields for automated detection and rollback.

Proposal (high level):
1) Naming scheme: KEY-{env}-{team}-{service}-{purpose}-{YYYYMMDD}-{rand4} (examples: KEY-prod-payments-ingest-epoch-20250314-A3F2). The name must include env and team.
2) Epochal cryptoperiods: default TTL 7 days for service tokens; 24 hours for ephemeral host-bound tokens; ability to request longer TTL (business-justified) via approvals and recorded in ticket metadata.
3) Host-bound ephemerals: integrate with Credential Broker to mint tokens that require a host fingerprint (instance-id/hostname + cert thumbprint). Tokens are unusable if presented from a different host.
4) Rotation enforcement: automated rotation cron for keys with <72 hours remaining; immediate rotate-and-revoke flow for suspected compromise. Rotation events must create immutable audit entries including prior_key_id, new_key_id, rotated_by, rotation_reason, and bounding metadata.
5) Backfill & migration: provide migration shim to mint host-bound tokens for selected services; legacy long-lived tokens flagged and scheduled for expiry.
6) Audit logging: extend audit schema to include token_label, token_id (opaque), cryptoperiod_start/end, host_fingerprint (if bound), request_source, and rotation_event_id. Logs should be shipped to central ELK/Snowflake with low-latency indexing for alerting.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Host-binding increases operational complexity for autoscaling groups. We will implement a lightweight agent-friendly fingerprint (instance-id + ephemeral agent cert) instead of strict hardware-bound attestation for initial rollout.
- Shorter TTLs reduce blast radius but increase load on the credential broker; we will add batching and token reuse heuristics to reduce churn (see Optimize: reuse window in implementation).
- Naming scheme is strict to help search and audits but requires a migration rename map for existing tokens present in live systems.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (P0 - infra & schema): extend Credential Broker API, audit schema changes, add naming enforcement on create. Add DB migrations and index audit fields.
Phase 2 (P1 - host-bound token): implement host_fingerprint binding, integrate with agent that can mint ephemeral certs, provide SDK helpers.
Phase 3 (P2 - rollout & migration): run targeted migration on low-risk infra, monitor errors, then broader rollout with staged expiry of legacy tokens.
Phase 4 (P3 - enforcement): enable blockers in token creation paths that prevent new long-lived tokens without approval; alert owners of legacy tokens.

Acceptance criteria:
- New tokens are created only using the naming scheme for 90% of creates within two weeks after rollout.
- Credential Broker issues host-bound ephemeral tokens; token misuse from non-bound host must be rejected in >95% simulated attempts.
- Audit pipeline surfaces rotation events with required structured fields and triggers detection rule that creates Slack alert for any emergency revoke.
- Migration script successfully replaces keys for three pilot services (payments-ingest, logs-forwarder, metrics-collector) without >1% increased error rate.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Alert if token churn (creates + rotates) exceeds baseline by 3x for more than 5 minutes.
- Alert for repeated authentication failures using host-bound tokens (possible agent misconfiguration).
- Dashboard: tokens-by-env, tokens-by-team, tokens-nearing-expiry, rotates-per-day.

Rollout plan and communications:
- Week 1: schema + broker changes behind feature flags; internal docs (Confluence) and SDK examples updated.
- Week 2: pilot with two infra teams, collect metrics, iterate agent.
- Week 3+: broader rollout with scheduled expiry windows and support rotations via on-call.
- Communications: Org-wide email and Slack channel #sec-token-migrations with runbook link.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: token creation failures during rollout breaking services. Mitigation: feature flags, gradual ramp, and automatic rollback hooks.
- Risk: increased load on credential broker. Mitigation: token reuse heuristics and batching; autoscale plans for broker.

References and links:

- GitHub PR (broker changes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/credential-broker/pull/612
- Migration scripts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-scripts/tree/main/token-migrations
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/tokens-overview

Next steps (this ticket):
- Approve naming and cryptoperiod defaults (security + infra).
- Kick off Phase 1 implementation tasks and open sub-issues for SDK, agent changes, and audit index migration.
